preconditions.text: Victim has deposited funds into the vault; victim holds a validator-granted self-allowance; withdraw()/redeem() accept an arbitrary owner parameter and verify only the owner's self-allowance via spendSelfAllowance(); any external account can call the functions without victim approval; and msg.sender differs from the supplied owner.
preconditions.derivation: Conjunction of the prior-state and static call-path observations extracted as preconditions; none asserts completion, state change, root cause, intent or impact. The code-match assumption (as_code_matches) cannot be expressed without exceeding the 8-symbol budget and is retained under assumptions instead of being dropped.
evidence: The `withdraw()` and `redeem()` functions in `WERC7575Vault.sol` accept an arbitrary `owner` parameter but only verify the owner's self-allowance via `spendSelfAllowance()`. They fail to check whether `msg.sender` is authorized by the owner, allowing any external account to steal funds from any user with active self-allowance.

The function accepts any `owner` address from any caller and only verifies that the `owner` has self-allowance (platform permission). There is no check that `msg.sender == owner` or that `allowance[owner][msg.sender] >= shares`.
Per ERC-4626, when `msg.sender != owner`, the vault MUST verify caller authorization. This check is completely absent.
Any external account can drain 100% of any user's vault deposits by calling:
- Victim has deposited funds into the vault
- Victim has self-allowance granted by validator (required for normal protocol operation)
No approval from victim required. No user interaction needed. Attack cost is only gas fees.

safety.text: When msg.sender differs from the supplied owner and the owner's vault position is spent, the caller is authorized by or on behalf of the owner, per the ERC-4626 caller-authorization requirement.
safety.derivation: Protected-effect shape effect->authorized taken from the security intent: spending the owner's self-allowance under msg.sender != owner implies caller authorization. Direction and negation preserved (antecedent is not-owner AND spent; consequent is authorized).

Per ERC-4626, when `msg.sender != owner`, the vault MUST verify caller authorization. This check is completely absent.

effects.text: The owner's vault position is spent (self-allowance consumed) while the caller is not authorized by or on behalf of the owner.
effects.derivation: Direct-impact facts restated independently: the victim's position is withdrawn without the owner's approval (spent AND not-authorized), which is exactly the effect-and-not-authorized form that falsifies the safety implication.
